title: Domain-Size-Dependent Residual Stress Governs the Phase-Transition and Photoluminescence Behavior of Methylammonium Lead Iodide

notes: Spine: conflicting PL reports -> domain-size/residual-stress hypothesis -> MAPbI3 base + PC/HOC/SC sweep + three growth routes -> crystallization -> domain size (F1a) and identical phase (F1b,c) -> state-dependent lattice expansion (F2a) -> inhomogeneous residual strain (F2d + Williamson-Hall) -> residual-stress MEC (Delta-V = 2.0%, F4c) -> surface-triggered shrinking-core transition (F4a,b) -> state-dependent PL (F3a) -> domain-size-dependent T_trans and window (F5a,b) -> conclusion. Control branch: fine grinding (F3b) removes the transition. Second branch: atmospheric ageing (F6) makes the SC surface PC-like, so PDPL gauges crystallinity. Audits: a1 blank 150-165 K band in the SC TDPL map, a2 the sigma(700 K) / sigma(100 K) normalisation conflict, a3 the dual-emission boundary sitting at 200-300 um rather than 500 um. Typing choice: n12 is STR/phase/fraction (degree of transformation with a spatial gradient) rather than STR/microstructure/distribution, because the next step is how much has transformed, not where a constituent lies. F2b and F2c (drawn (004) and (242) plane models) are not cited: they carry no readout. Not in the graph: supporting-information items (Figures S2-S5, S13-S15, S17) that the linked text leans on, including the XPS carbon depth profile behind the surface-disruption claim, and the 100 um PC comparison of Figure S13.
